newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-BARCELONA CONFIRM VAN GAAL AS NEW COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BARCELONA CONFIRM VAN GAAL AS NEW COACH.

text.p: Barcelona confirmed on Monday that Ajax Amsterdam boss Louis van Gaal would take over from Bobby Robson as coach for the next three seasons.
An official at the Spanish first division club said former England manager Robson had agreed "in principle" to stay as technical director, with special responsibility for signing players.
The official said Van Gaal would be formally presented on Monday at 4.30 pm (1430 gmt).
In the coming week the club is expected to announce the signing of several players chosen by the new coach.
Dutch defender Michael Reiziger and French striker Christian Dugarry are both likely to move to Barcelona from AC Milan.
In his time at Dutch club Ajax, van Gaal built up a side from largely home-grown talent that looked likely to dominate the European game for several years.
But after beating AC Milan in the 1995 European Cup final, Ajax fell to Juventus at the final hurdle in 1996 and struggled in last season's competition with the departure of key players.
Van Gaal said earlier in the season he would not stay on at Ajax, and that he had reached agreement with a major European club he refused to name.
Van Gaal had been linked to Barcelona since the end of fellow Dutchman Johan Cruyff's eight-year spell in charge of the club.
Cruyff was sacked in May last year, and Robson was hurriedly brought to the Camp Nou from Portugal's Porto.

But despite winning the Spanish Cup, the European Cup Winners' Cup and the Spanish Super Cup in Robson's first season, Barcelona played second fiddle to arch-rivals Real Madrid in the league, and fans quickly turned against the English coach.
